question: Elite athletes' bodies became far more varied during the twentieth century. Why, according to Epstein?
options: Each sport selected its ideal body
answer: Because each sport began to select its ideal body. Early in the century, the average shot-putter and high jumper looked alike; as sport grew professional and global, tall, long-armed people gravitated to swimming and basketball, and small ones to gymnastics. Epstein calls it the Big Bang of body types.
move: When selection gets tougher, the people selected grow more extreme.
trap: 'Diet made everyone taller': people did grow, so it seems enough.
simply: A hundred years ago, athletes in different sports looked similar. Now each sport picks people built for it: tall swimmers, tiny gymnasts.
why: Extreme results at the top often say more about who was selected than about what training did, a useful check on any 'secret of champions'.
reference: David Epstein, The Sports Gene: Inside the Science of Extraordinary Athletic Performance (Current, 2013), ch. 7
